svg.text: Why a buffer, not a pipe?
A bowed row crosses up to 10 lines
either side: all in memory at once.
free until the writer comes round again
A slot lives for 64 machine lines = 2.9 ms, and the output needs it for at most about 22 of them. The rest is slack,
so the writer never catches up with the reader. (One line takes 44.8 µs; in the animation a step takes 0.2 s.)
The ring is sized for the strongest bend the module supports (10 lines either side).
The board uses k = 1/32 (about 3 %), so in practice fewer slots are being drawn at once.
